title: Mason County approves hyperscale data center in deal with Meta
key_facts: The Mason County Fiscal Court in Kentucky voted unanimously on Tuesday (13 Oct 2026) to approve a resolution moving forward with a hyperscale data center, contracting with Meta.
Officials said the project could bring billions in investment and be the largest data center in Kentucky so far.
County officials expect 2,000 construction and trades jobs and a guaranteed minimum of 400 permanent jobs.

Attorney Jim Parsons said the initial investment will be around $15 billion, paying for water and sewer improvements, a new plant for the city of Maysville, a public safety payment and a $750,000 payment to the county that does not depend on construction being completed.
The agreement spans a 40-year, multi-phase plan that could see up to $800 billion invested.
Judge-Executive Owen McNeill said it will generate tens of millions of dollars for the county and its schools and could allow lower taxes.
Construction of the initial phase is expected to begin within three years.
quote_evidence: The Mason County Fiscal Court voted unanimously Tuesday to approve a resolution moving forward with plans for a hyperscale data center, contracting with Meta.
Attorney Jim Parsons said the initial investment will be around $15 billion.
Construction for the initial phase is expected to begin within the next three years following Tuesday’s agreement.
why_it_matters_hint: A rural Kentucky county has backed a very large Meta data center plan, with officials claiming big jobs and revenue gains.
notes: Single local TV outlet. Article is clumsy in places (a garbled sentence on the project, 'Mayesville' spelling); the $800 billion figure is given without a named speaker, so it is attributed to WKYT. The project is described as 'if executed'.
